children: A New Mexico lawyer was fined $5000 after a court found that a murder appeal he filed contained fabricated witnesses and false police testimony generated with help from ChatGPT

The New Mexico Supreme Court held attorney Stephen Aarons in contempt Wednesday and referred him to an attorney disciplinary board for investigation. The court said his filing included fictional statements, including an account that the shooter wore dark pants and a white shirt.
Aarons told Reuters that he used ChatGPT

to summarize a computer-generated trial transcript and other case materials after taking over the appeal last year. He said he had assumed the technology would produce a reliable summary and did not understand the extent to which it could invent facts.
“I am remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake,” Aarons said.
The appeal concerns Oscar Renee Sandoval, who was convicted of murdering the mother of his children and sentenced to life in prison. The appeal remains pending.

The justices criticized Aarons for failing to verify the material before submitting it. Justice C. Shannon Bacon questioned how unfamiliar he could have been with the risks of AI-generated errors, describing such problems as widely reported.
The court also said Aarons showed insufficient concern for his client.

title: Lawyer fined after ChatGPT use in New Mexico murder appeal
